title: Black images, NaN and grey mush
hook: One bad number can turn a whole picture black, and nothing tells you. How NaN gets in, why it spreads, and the flags that really exist.

verified.claim: At denoise 0.25 and 20 steps on SD 1.5 sigmas, the start sigma was 0.231 for karras, 0.671 for normal and 0.693 for simple.
SaveImage turned a NaN image into pixels of 0, 0, 0, with the warning: invalid value encountered in cast. Values of 5 and -5 became 255 and 0.
verified.ref: nodes.py:SaveImage.save_images on a CPU, read back from the PNG

verified.claim: No check for NaN in core's sampling code, nodes.py or comfy_extras' sampling nodes stops a run.
verified.ref: a search for isnan and nan_to_num in comfy/*.py, comfy/k_diffusion and nodes.py

verified.claim: --fp16-vae, --bf16-vae, --fp32-vae, --cpu-vae, --force-fp32 and --force-upcast-attention exist, and the help for two of them mentions black images.
A VAE's dtype comes from vae_dtype: a flag first, then the first dtype in working_dtypes that the card suits, then fp32. The default list is bf16, then fp32.
--force-fp32 makes should_use_fp16 and should_use_bf16 return False.
The SDXL VAE makes NaNs in fp16 because internal activation values are too big, according to its fp16-fix model card.
The lcm render on SD 1.5: edge measure 6.51 against euler's 20.17, one seed.

unchecked: We didn't reproduce a black image from a real VAE in fp16. The source and the model card say it happens, and the lab shows the arithmetic only.
We didn't render a wrong-VAE or low-denoise picture for this lesson. What they look like is labelled in the prose as expectation, from the numbers.
We don't know of a complete list of what causes NaN in sampling. This covers what we could check.
